quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front of you suddenly slows down or stops.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front of you suddenly slows down or stops.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front of you suddenly slows down or stops, you may not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let other cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. If you are on a two-lane road and driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: This sign shape and color indicates a ____ sign.
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to show a no passing zone.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle coming toward you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass by moving to the right side of the road and stopping. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side of the road.

questions.question: A driver approaching a flashing red light must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane show where a crosswalk is. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible for staying out of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side:

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before going.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before going.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks side by side, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand point upward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points upward, it means they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: If you hit a parked car, you need to:

options.text: Wait at the scene until the owner comes back.
Try to find the owner, or leave a note with your name, phone number, and the time and date of the crash.
Leave your name and address at the county courthouse.
Call a tow truck to take the car away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to find the owner, or leave a note with your name, phone number, and the time and date of the crash.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a note in a visible place with your contact information and the date and time of the crash.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes. Where are they found?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to whom?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout when entering.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right side of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle using its lights and siren.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before going.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before going.
questions.explanation: Do not move when a train passes. Wait until you can see down all tracks clearly before crossing.

questions.question: Why should you be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than larger vehicles.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. Many collisions happen because drivers were looking but did not see them. Stay alert to these road users.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: You react more slowly to hazards.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: At high speeds, how far behind the vehicle in front should you stay to stop safely?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: At speeds above 30 mph, keep a four-second distance behind the vehicle in front. This gives you enough time to stop safely in an emergency.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right lane immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: Return to the right side of the road when you have enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risk of crashing due to alcohol?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If a yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross them to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert drivers that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs and never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What should you do when passing a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road?

options.text: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver may open the door as you approach. Use extra caution around parked cars.
